title: Sign in securely
goal: Open your permitted VAS workspace.
steps: Enter your issued Username. The demonstration account shown is not a production login.
Enter your Password. It is case sensitive.
Select Continue securely. Follow Change Password if your account requires rotation.
expected: An authenticated workspace or the required password-change screen opens. The test administrator reached Change Password.
recovery: For a security block, ask the administrator to check the allowed HTTPS origin and account status. Use the approved server address; do not disable browser security.

title: Complete first-login password rotation
goal: Replace the administrator-issued password before continuing.
steps: Enter CURRENT PASSWORD: the password just used to sign in.
Enter NEW PASSWORD. The screen requires at least 12 characters and at least 6 different characters.
Re-enter it in CONFIRM NEW PASSWORD.
Select CHANGE PASSWORD. If a success message appears, acknowledge it.
expected: The workspace opens; the new password works on the next login. Both the synthetic administrator and standard user completed rotation.
recovery: If confirmation does not match, correct both new-password fields. Rotation signs out other sessions; sign back in there.

title: Find the correct workspace
role: Administrator; standard users see fewer links
goal: Use the actual navigation instead of guessing page addresses.
steps: Open MANAGEMENT to reveal its menu.
Select Known Faces to open the people directory. Use the equivalent entries under SEARCH & INTELLIGENCE or SYSTEM for their workspaces.
expected: The selected page opens and the active navigation changes. HOME is administrator-only; LIVE FEEDS is the operator detection view.
recovery: Missing menu items can reflect permissions. A direct administrator URL redirected the tested standard user to Live Pipeline Feeds.
limit: LAF-AI is a separate application link. Its SSO launch was not tested.

title: Read Home and camera summaries
goal: Check the overview and focus on a registered camera.
steps: Select Refresh to reload the summary.
Choose a camera in the pipeline selector further down the page.
expected: Counts and the selected camera context are displayed. Synthetic cameras and observations were visible in the overview.
recovery: If a camera is absent, check that its sender has registered it through ingestion and that data falls within the visible scope.

title: Review live detection feeds
role: Active account; permitted pipelines for non-administrators
goal: Review the latest stored detections for accessible cameras.
steps: Select Open recent detections to expand the recent-detection area.
expected: Detection cards show snapshots, names or unknown status, similarity and timing. The restricted user saw only the assigned demonstration camera.
recovery: CONNECTED describes the page connection, not camera/model health. If cards are stale, check upstream VMS publishing and ingest health before changing recognition thresholds.
limit: No physical camera stream or newly recognized face was used. This page is a detection/snapshot feed, not a verified continuous-video player. Sound controls were observed; audio and notification delivery were not tested.

title: Filter unknown identities and open evidence
goal: Find an unknown record in the correct camera scope.
steps: Choose Pipeline. The example uses the demonstration entrance camera.
Set Min Appearances. Leave 1 to include records with at least one appearance.
Select Apply filters.
Select VIEW & ALERT on the desired identity card.
expected: The list is restricted to the chosen camera and Identity Details opens. Date From/Date To further narrow the scope; Reset filters restores the form.
recovery: Check the date range, pipeline and minimum count before concluding that data is missing. SHOW ALL (>24h hidden) broadens the normal recent listing.

title: Follow a recorded movement journey
role: Account permitted to view the identity
goal: Connect camera visits to the corresponding saved photos.
steps: Select Journey overview to see visit groups and time gaps.
Select Every sighting · camera lanes to switch to individual observations.
Select a numbered sighting to update the linked photo and timestamp.
Use Next sighting (the right-arrow control) to advance one observation.
Select Enlarge on the photo.
Use Next → in the photo viewer to review another stored appearance.
Select Close × to return to the journey.
expected: The selected number, camera, time and photo change together. Fifteen seeded sightings across three cameras were navigated in the test.
recovery: A gap is time without a recorded sighting. It does not show where the person was. A missing image should be checked against storage and retention.
limit: This is recorded-sighting review, not recorded-video playback, continuous GPS tracking or evidence of motion between cameras. Review sequence advances still images.

title: Find and rename a known-person record
goal: Update a display name and verify the identity profile.
steps: Enter the name or person ID in Search directory.
Select Manage person on the matching card.
Edit the name field.
Select Save name and acknowledge any success message.
Select Open full profile to verify the saved name and identity details.
expected: The profile showed Demo Person 01 - Training after saving. The identity UUID and history remain associated with the same record.
recovery: Use the stable identity ID when names are similar. Add photo, Deactivate person and Permanently delete are separate operations; renaming does not perform them.

title: Prepare enrollment or identity review
start: Known faces → Add person; or an unknown identity’s detail dialog
goal: Understand the available review controls before an identity-changing action.
steps: From an unknown detail dialog, open PROMOTE TO KNOWN to inspect the review form.
Use MERGE only when reviewing records already confirmed to represent the same person; review the proposed source and survivor before any submission.
expected: Promotion review was opened. Add person was also observed. Successful photo enrollment, promotion and merge were not executed for this guide.
recovery: Use approved face images for enrollment. A matching score or similar-looking card is not identity confirmation. Cancel an uncertain decision.
limit: The demonstration avatars are deliberately not face photographs. No real person was identified. Merge suggestions, bulk merge, image replacement, deactivation and permanent deletion remain unexecuted.

title: Prepare a photo enrollment
goal: Understand the required enrollment inputs without bypassing review.
steps: Enter PERSON NAME.
Choose PHOTO or drag an approved image onto the upload area. The dialog accepts JPEG, JPG, PNG and WEBP up to 10 MB.
Use THIS IS A FACE IMAGE (ALREADY CROPPED) only for a genuine cropped face; otherwise leave it unchecked.
Select UPLOAD PERSON only after validating the inputs and authorization.
expected: A successful enrollment should complete its review and appear in Known faces with a usable photo. This guide did not submit an enrollment or claim that success.
recovery: For no-face or quality errors, provide a suitable approved photo. Do not use the cropped-face option to bypass an invalid image.
limit: The synthetic avatars are unsuitable biometric enrollment images. Final candidate/duplicate review and recognition were not verified.

title: Submit an image search and handle a quality failure
goal: Set image-search scope and distinguish invalid input from no matches.
steps: Choose the reference image using the upload area.
Select Search Scope.
Set Max Results Per Face.
Select Quality Check to inspect whether the image is usable.
Select Search only with a usable approved image.
expected: The synthetic avatar produced “Quality check failed: No face was detected in the image.” A search completed with zero detected faces and zero results, and appeared in Search History.
recovery: Replace a no-face image with an approved, clear face photo. Broaden overly restrictive camera/date filters only when appropriate. Do not interpret invalid input as proof that a person is absent.
limit: Positive biometric matching, batch success, result-image export and recognition accuracy were not validated.

title: Filter search history and export CSV
role: Administrator; authorization to export the selected records
goal: Review prior searches and download an authorized history file.
steps: Choose Search Type.
Select the Days Back range.
Select APPLY FILTERS.
Select EXPORT to open Export Search History.
Choose CSV under EXPORT FORMAT and review DATE RANGE.
Select EXPORT in the dialog.
expected: The browser downloaded a CSV and VAS displayed “History exported successfully!” The test file contained synthetic search history only.
recovery: Check the browser download area if no file appears. Verify format, date range and row content before sharing. Clear history changes stored history and was not used.

title: Create a watchlist
goal: Create a named monitoring list.
steps: Enter Name, for example Demo Review List.
Enter a Description explaining its approved purpose.
Select Alert Level. The example uses Info (Low Priority).
Select Save Watchlist.
expected: The list appeared with its name and active state. Search, level, status and sort controls help find it later.
recovery: A name alone does not enroll members. Use the identity’s Add to Watchlist workflow. Alert level expresses urgency, not a probability of wrongdoing.

title: Add an identity to a watchlist and check membership
goal: Save membership with review context.
steps: Choose Select Watchlist.
Select Priority.
Enter Notes.
Enter Action Instructions, if appropriate.
Select Add to Watchlist.
Reload the profile and inspect WATCHLISTS; also verify the member inside the named watchlist’s View panel.
expected: The membership save returned success and the named list’s member view contained the synthetic identity. The profile chip displayed “Untitled watchlist” in this build.
recovery: If the chip is untitled, verify the member in Watchlist Management instead of repeatedly adding it. Report the display issue with the identity/list IDs.

title: Create, inspect and pause a live-alert rule
role: Administrator for this tested workflow; permitted identity
goal: Save a rule, inspect readiness, and pause it without sending a test notification.
steps: Enter Alert Name.
Select Alert severity.
Set Minimum Similarity for the approved use case.
Review Notify on dashboard, Sound alert and Auto-capture snapshot. Sound was disabled in the demonstration.
Select Create Alert.
Open Live Alerts and select Health on the saved rule.
Select Pause when the demonstration is complete.
expected: The rule was created; Health showed channel and identity checks; Pause changed the saved state to PAUSED and offered Resume.
recovery: Health reported SNAPSHOT EXISTS: PROBLEM in the isolated fixture, although the profile photo rendered. Investigate that check before relying on delivery. Test can send notifications and was not used.
limit: No alert trigger, browser audio, acknowledgement, email or SMS delivery was tested. Cameras displayed All in this form’s saved rule; do not assume a camera selector exists here.

title: Save a camera’s display location
role: Administrator; camera already registered by ingestion
goal: Maintain the location used in investigation and map views.
steps: Select Edit Location on the intended pipeline.
Enter Location Name.
Enter Latitude between -90 and 90.
Enter Longitude between -180 and 180.
Select Save Location.
Select Refresh and verify the same location remains.
expected: The demonstration name persisted after refresh. Coordinates can be entered even when the basemap is unavailable.
recovery: VAS pipelines are registered by ingestion; this page is not an RTSP camera-discovery wizard. Rename changes the pipeline identifier and keeps an alias; that operation was not exercised.

title: Create a camera-scoped user
goal: Create a standard account with explicitly assigned camera access.
steps: Select Create New User.
Enter Username.
Enter Email address; the demonstration uses the reserved example.test domain.
Enter a temporary Password that meets policy.
Select Role. USER - Standard Access was tested.
Select only the required Pipeline access checkboxes. Keep the account active; grant Chatbot access only when needed.
Select Save user and acknowledge the confirmation.
Check the saved row, role, pipeline count and MUST CHANGE PASSWORD indicator.
expected: The synthetic user logged in, rotated its password and saw only its assigned camera. Opening /admin/users as that user returned it to Live Pipeline Feeds.
recovery: Administrator assignment was disabled in this form. Observer and Analyzer options were visible but their full permission boundaries were not tested. The system account is protected and non-login.

title: Issue an ingest credential for an authorized sender
goal: Create a sender-specific credential and preserve it securely.
steps: Enter the sender name in the credential-name field.
Select Issue token.
Use Copy token to transfer the one-time token to the authorized sender’s secret store. The token is permanently redacted in this guide.
Dismiss the token dialog only after securing it.
Check the sender’s row in Issued credentials.
expected: A synthetic sender credential was issued and appeared in the list. The full token is shown once; the guide does not contain it.
recovery: If the token is lost, follow the administrator’s replacement/revocation procedure. Last-used timestamps can lag; absence of a recent time is not immediate proof of failure.
limit: No real sender was configured; webhook delivery and revocation were not tested. Static legacy ingest keys and sender-specific bearer tokens are different authentication methods.

title: Edit a setting and verify its application timing
goal: Change one permitted value and verify the reported result.
steps: Search for Search history retention.
Select Edit on the matching setting.
Enter NEW VALUE. The example extends the period from 90 to 120 days in the isolated instance.
Enter CHANGE REASON.
Select Save Changes.
Select REFRESH and check the value and application hint.
expected: The setting showed 120 days after refresh. The editor states that this setting applies at the next scheduled job run.
recovery: Saved does not always mean immediately effective. Read In use, saved-value differences and restart/next-job hints. Security-critical settings may be read-only.

title: Preview retention cleanup without deleting data
goal: Estimate eligible cleanup and verify job completion.
steps: Select Refresh Retention Status.
Select Run Retention Dry Test.
Filter Execution history with “retention” and open the completed dry-run task if further detail is needed.
expected: Data Retention Dry Run reached COMPLETED. It counts what would be deleted and does not delete records.
recovery: A submitted job is not a completed job: wait for its final state. Do not choose Run Retention Now for a preview. Retention age and cleanup interval mean different things.

title: Review chatbot query audit
goal: Narrow investigation evidence without clearing it.
steps: Choose USERNAME in Refine activity.
Choose STATUS.
Select Apply filters.
Choose Rows per page at the bottom of the table.
Select Next only when another page is available.
expected: The page displayed Chatbot audit log and no query records in the isolated run. This page audits chatbot queries and responses, not every administrative action.
recovery: Check user, date and status filters. An empty query log is expected when no assistant query has completed.
limit: Query-detail and response inspection could not be verified without completed assistant queries.

title: Filter application logs
goal: Narrow the loaded log records without clearing them.
steps: Choose LOG LEVEL, for example ERROR.
Select Apply Filters.
Use Find on this page to narrow the loaded records.
expected: The ERROR query returned No logs found in the scanned scope. Source, dates and Per Page change that scope.
recovery: Reset overly narrow filters and select Refresh. An empty filtered page does not prove the absence of errors. Do not clear logs needed for investigation.
limit: Sensitive log export and log clearing were not performed.

title: Build a social relationship graph
role: Administrator; observations for the selected scope
goal: Inspect coappearance connections and their provenance.
steps: Set DAYS BACK; leave identities empty only when analysis of every accessible identity is intended.
Select ANALYZE NETWORK.
Inspect the graph, node/connection counts and provenance.
expected: The synthetic dataset returned 14 nodes, 91 connections and one cluster. The result identified the rules/co-occurrence engine.
recovery: Open Select Identities to restrict the analysis. A connection means observed coappearance under the selected rules, not proof of a personal relationship or coordination.

title: Review suspicious-pattern output
goal: Scope pattern detection and inspect the returned evidence.
steps: Choose the pipeline scope.
Set DAYS BACK; review MIN GROUP SIZE.
Select DETECT PATTERNS.
Review the returned cards and use VIEW DETAILS when investigating a specific result.
expected: The synthetic history produced group-activity cards with locations, times and identity counts.
recovery: Large groups in demonstration data are manufactured examples. Empty output, scores and “confidence” labels require evidence review; they are not validated probabilities of misconduct.
status: Tested — result generation; detail review limited

title: Check anomalies and recover from insufficient history
goal: Choose a subject and test whether a usable baseline exists.
steps: In the picker, search by name or ID.
Select the intended result.
Set DAYS BACK.
Select DETECT ANOMALIES.
Read the baseline/evidence message before interpreting the output.
expected: The test returned “Insufficient baseline”: all 15 appearances were inside the 90-day window, leaving zero earlier appearances; at least five were required.
recovery: Use a shorter window only when it leaves sufficient earlier observations, or collect more history. Do not treat a baseline failure as “no anomalies”.

title: Assess threat evidence and provenance
goal: Read a persisted rules-based assessment with its limitations.
steps: Choose the intended identity.
Select ASSESS THREAT.
Review risk factors, baseline warnings, Requested mode, Executed mode and Final scoring.
expected: The test returned a moderate score of 25.0 from connection count, with an insufficient-anomaly-baseline warning and rules provenance.
recovery: The interface explicitly describes risk-engine-v1 as a heuristic score, not a probability. Record outcome creates a consequential review label and was not used.

title: Check advanced analytics readiness
goal: Distinguish enabled controls from working dependencies and sufficient evidence.
steps: Use Review saved thresholds to inspect existing candidates rather than learning or activating new ones.
Select CHECK FEATURE STATUS.
Read the per-feature readiness details.
expected: The report showed ready network/pattern/anomaly/threat functions, threshold learning with a worker unavailable, and unavailable security zones/maps. Trajectory and correlation were available subject to per-case evidence.
recovery: Enabled does not mean usable for every identity. Trajectory requires at least three outgoing sessions; correlation is heuristic association. Threshold candidates need separate review and activation.
limit: Learning/activating thresholds, trajectory execution, correlation execution and Learn All Camera Thresholds were not completed.

title: Diagnose a missing map
goal: Load spatial evidence or identify the missing basemap dependency.
steps: Select the identity.
Choose MAP STYLE from the available styles.
Select LOAD MAP.
expected: The isolated instance reported missing/unavailable basemap support. Camera coordinates could still be saved separately.
recovery: Ask the administrator to verify installed offline map archives, content checks and the map service. No coordinates should be invented to make an empty map look populated.
limit: Basemap rendering, terrain/satellite layers, zones, heatmaps and continuous route accuracy were not verified.

title: Follow the ML service lifecycle and readiness gate
role: Administrator; healthy worker and suitable data for actual training
goal: Use the current four-stage service workflow.
steps: Choose Service: Behavior assessment, Pair relationships, Social network, Analyst review queue or Numeric experiments.
Inspect Prepare & train and the readiness message before submitting a run.
Expand Inspect data & notebook to locate the service’s inspection controls. Availability of a control does not prove a notebook was executed.
expected: The interface exposes Train → Review → Connect → Monitor. In this isolated instance the worker was unavailable and training remained disabled.
recovery: Use Refresh status and Advanced tools & troubleshooting to diagnose worker/data requirements. A prepared dataset or candidate is not an active production decision model.
limit: Training, metrics, tuning, model connection, drift and notebook execution were not completed. Current visible provenance says rules make live decisions; model observations must not be described as autonomous threat decisions.

title: Locate database and notebook inspection tools
start: ML Operations → Advanced tools & troubleshooting → Inspect a dataset or model → Inspect existing database data
goal: Locate evidence-inspection controls and understand the current gap.
steps: Choose Data, such as Recognition observations or Identity sightings.
Enter Start (UTC).
Enter End (UTC), keeping the interval at most seven days; select the intended cameras when available.
Select Preview existing data.
expected: Expected in a working inspector: source rows/counts and an inspection-notebook download. In this run camera choices and default dates did not populate and Preview returned no visible result.
recovery: Report the initialization/dependency issue; do not claim that extraction or training succeeded. Inspect data & notebook for the selected ML service also requires actual dataset/run evidence.
limit: The guide does not supply a fabricated executed notebook or label synthetic fixture counts as an extracted training dataset.

title: Check similarity-model readiness
goal: Read the supervised merge-feedback requirements.
steps: Select Refresh.
Read the disabled training control and Dataset Readiness checks.
expected: The test showed Not Trained, Runtime Loaded: No, 0/50 samples, 0/5 approved, 0/5 rejected and 0/10 unique pairs.
recovery: Collect and review legitimate feedback in the approved process. Do not approve/reject pairs just to fill training counts. The page describes a heuristic or legacy fallback until a candidate is activated.

title: Use assistant help and recognize degraded mode
goal: Locate the conversational interface and verify service readiness.
steps: Enter a question in Message Surveillance AI only when the assistant is ready.
Use Send message to submit an approved query; this was not exercised against an available language model.
Select Help for the built-in instructions.
expected: The interface and Help opened, but the test displayed Assistant degraded. No model answer was represented as verified.
recovery: Ask the administrator to check configured model availability and read-only query dependencies. Review factual answers against underlying records before acting.
limit: Conversation generation, branching, feedback and generated report artifacts were not completed. No external assistant service was contacted.

title: Read the in-app tutorial
goal: Find guidance delivered by the running build.
steps: Select SYSTEM WORKFLOW or the relevant tutorial topic.
expected: The tutorial opened and reported application version 5.0.0. Topic navigation is available in the running interface.
recovery: Some Further reading entries refer to legacy document filenames. Use this guide’s verified workflow and current documentation index if a referenced file is absent.
